background_notes.fact: For every real q,a,r, S_a is an isometric linear bijection on H^q, preserves the zero Fourier coefficient, and S_(a+r)=S_a S_r.

grounds.reason: H^q is the weighted l2 Fourier completion.

background_notes.justification: Each multiplier has modulus one, so every weighted squared Fourier coefficient and its sum are unchanged. Multiplication of the scalar exponentials gives the group law; the multiplier at k=0 is one. The inverse is S_(-a). These identities extend from polynomials through the isometric completion.

background_notes.fact: A continuous path which is C1 on each closed piece of a finite compact time partition, with values in the smooth periodic functions, lies in L^infinity L2 and has weak derivative in L^infinity H^(-23/14) equal almost everywhere to its piecewise classical derivative.

grounds.reason: X uses the L-infinity norms and weak time derivative.
The initial Ctri domain has smooth spatial inputs with piecewise smooth continuous time dependence.
These are exactly the time-dependent paths to which E003 is applied.

background_notes.justification: Continuity on each compact piece bounds the path and its derivative in the indicated spaces. Integrating by parts against a smooth compactly supported scalar time test function on each piece gives the distributional derivative. Adjacent endpoint terms cancel by continuity, so there are no delta masses at the partition points. A finite maximum bounds the derivative essential supremum.

background_notes.fact: A bilinear or trilinear map on dense subspaces of Banach input spaces, satisfying ||T(x_1,...,x_m)||<=K product_j||x_j|| with values in a complete normed space, has a unique continuous multilinear extension with the same bound. Here the constant-input Ctri bounds and permitted E004 stage bounds extend from mean-zero trigonometric polynomials to the displayed Sobolev spaces; the same principle applies to closures of any specified initial path domain in its controlling norm.

grounds.reason: The Sobolev spaces are completions of trigonometric polynomials, and the zero Fourier coefficient can be deleted to preserve mean zero.
Ctri is trilinear on its initial domain.
Fstage is bilinear on its initial domain.
E003 supplies the constant-input trilinear bound.
E004 supplies the bilinear bound for permitted source parameters.

background_notes.justification: For approximating input sequences, expand the difference of two outputs as a sum of m terms, each containing one input difference. The product bound and boundedness of convergent input sequences make the outputs Cauchy. Completeness yields a limit; the same difference bound makes it independent of approximants and proves continuity, multilinearity and the original estimate. Fourier truncation is dense in each H^q by convergence of its defining weighted l2 series. This does not assert density of smooth paths in the entirety of an L-infinity derivative space.

background_notes.fact: For smooth time-independent mean-zero f,g and a<=t, Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=S_(-a) Fstage_(0,t-a)(S_a f,S_a g). The same identity holds on the bounded Sobolev extensions furnished by the permitted E004 estimates.

grounds.reason: The Fourier multiplier gives the S group law and boundedness.
Fstage is one half the time integral of B_s.
The proof establishes B_(a+r)(f,g)=S_(-a)B_r(S_a f,S_a g).

background_notes.justification: Insert the group law into B, substitute s=a+r in its smooth time integral, and pass the fixed bounded linear map S_(-a) through the integral. These operations are valid in every fixed Sobolev space for the smooth integrand on a compact interval. Apply the continuous multilinear extension principle of BG003 to pass this identity to H^gamma inputs. No source mesh with nonzero a is assumed.
